author: potuz
content: I think this attack gets to be considerable worse or at least more subtle depending on design decisions on PQ because the IL could potentially lead to the victim builders to carry more aggregations on top of simulations, while the attacking builder doesn't care at all cause it just invalidates all txs immediately

author: vladimir_ea
content: Right. I guess the question is what the maximum amount of additional work is that can be imposed on a builder by an IL. The simulation cost of different transactions can vary greatly from microseconds to 10s of milliseconds.

author: vladimir_ea
content: (and for context having to sim multiple txs that take 10s of millis each for every block built would significantly reduce a builders competitiveness)

author: vladimir_ea
content: This doesn't actually require any collusion: a builder can receive the IL, simulate the txs, and if any turn out to be costly to sim in terms of latency,  include a cheap invalidating tx and thereby hope to gain an advantage over other builders who do try to correctly include the txs in the IL.

author: vladimir_ea
content: (assuming it is possible to create an invalidating tx? maybe that part does require collusion)

author: soispoke
content: I agree we just need to make sure the additional work is bounded properly (which shouldn't be too hard, we could just have per IL and per IL txn limits)

author: soispoke
content: if you don't assume collusion the attack is riskier and based on IL building rules (your txns need to pay N amount of fees to ensure they'll be included in ILs + they need to be submitted N slots before because they're also weighted by time spent in the mempool)

author: vladimir_ea
content: is it the case that transactions should be selected for ILs based on how long they have been in the mempool? i.e. to include the txs that are not otherwise being included;  or is it based on fees? or is it up to the includer?  b/c you could just systematically seed the mempool with low paying 'sim-bomb' txs and wait for them to show up in ILs.

author: soispoke
content: the original idea was: a combination of fees, time spent in mempool and transaction size while letting clients choose the exact rule they were going to implement (to have a bit of diversity across clients)

author: soispoke
content: it's not up to the includer unless they modify client code

author: vladimir_ea
content: one mitigation would be to enforce a gas limit for a tx included in an IL

author: vladimir_ea
content: without a limit the IL can be used adversarially and its a real problem

author: soispoke
content: yes that's what I meant by per IL and per IL txn gas limits

author: vladimir_ea
content: So in the spec is it that a builder is not obliged to include an IL tx that uses > X gas?

author: vladimir_ea
content: Even if > X gas remains in the block?
